data_schema: 23 raw columns including transaction time, merchant/category, amount, customer/geography and target is_fraud. The first CSV column is read by pandas as Unnamed: 0. Test features contain 22 columns; holdout labels are stored separately for independent review.
extra_notes: Use the local NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU with 8 GB VRAM. Train candidates sequentially: LightGBM on CPU, XGBoost with device='cuda' and tree_method='hist', and CatBoost with task_type='GPU'. The primary metric is PR-AUC (sklearn average_precision_score); also record F1, Recall, Precision, Brier score and an OOF-derived decision threshold. Use chronological validation based on trans_date_trans_time or unix_time, never a random split that leaks future behavior. Drop direct identifiers and PII-like memorization columns such as cc_num, trans_num, first, last, street; derive bounded time, amount, age and geo-distance features. Use native or ordinal categorical handling without dense one-hot expansion. Keep pandas memory bounded with selected columns/dtypes and release fold intermediates. Write sample_submission-compatible is_fraud probabilities for the full independent holdout. Never submit to a public leaderboard.
